entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-px8p-9vwx-vf98: fflate unzipSync can enter an infinite loop when parsing malformed ZIP64 archives
entry.content:
fflate unzipSync can enter an infinite loop when parsing malformed ZIP64 archives

Aliases: CVE-2026-45820

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H · CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N/E:U/S:N/AU:Y/R:U/V:D/RE:M/U:Amber

Affected:

  • fflate — fixed in 0.4.9
  • fflate — fixed in 0.5.4
  • fflate — fixed in 0.6.11
  • fflate — fixed in 0.7.5
  • fflate — fixed in 0.8.3

fflate through 0.8.2 is vulnerable to denial of service via an infinite loop in unzipSync(). A crafted ZIP archive with a central directory entry declaring compressed_size=0xFFFFFFFF (ZIP64 sentinel) but missing the required ZIP64 extra field tag 0x0001 causes z64e() to loop indefinitely due to out-of-bounds reads returning undefined, which coerces to 0, keeping the loop condition permanently true.

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-78x9-fhhx-v2g6: CKAN MCP Server: Cache-key canonicalization collision enables cache confusion / poisoning
entry.content:
CKAN MCP Server: Cache-key canonicalization collision enables cache confusion / poisoning

Aliases: CVE-2026-73846

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • @aborruso/ckan-mcp-server — fixed in 0.4.112

## Summary The response cache derives its key from an ambiguous string serialization of the request parameters. `canonicalizeParams` joins sorted `${key}=${value}` pairs with `&` and does not escape `&`, `=`, or the `|` field separators used in `buildCacheKey`. Two **different** logical parameter sets can therefore serialize to the **same** key and share one cache entry. Because the cached value is whatever the upstream returned for whichever request populated the entry first, an attacker can prime a colliding key so a victim's distinct query (same `server_url`) is served the attacker's cached response. ## Affected code ```js // src/utils/cache.ts export function canonicalizeParams(params) { const keys = Object.keys(params).sort(); const pairs = []; for (const key of keys) { c…
